question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution:
The correct answer is '**as**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage describes people waving and smiling "as" he passed by, indicating the action occurring at the same time.
 
• "**As**" is used to indicate a particular point in time during the action described.
 
• "Nor", "So", and "Thus" do not fit the context as they do not convey the simultaneous nature of the actions.
 
• "As" properly connects the actions of waving and smiling to his passing by.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

 

**Complete Passage**: He knew everyone on the island. Whenever his car stopped, half a dozen voices ***would ***__shout out his name. Policemen, agricultural labourers of low social status and priests waved and smiled __***____as___***__ he passed; everyone greeted him as a brother. They respected his honesty, and belligerence, and above all, they adored his typically Greek scorn and fearlessness when dealing with any _____ 3 ____ of Governmental red tape. On arrival, two of our cases containing linen and other things had been ______ 4 ____ by the Customs on the curious ground that they were merchandise. So, when we moved out to the villa and the problem of bed linen arose, Mother told Spiro ______ 5 _____ our cases in the Customs and asked for his advice.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Nor (और नहीं): Used to indicate a negative addition to a previous statement, not a simultaneous action.
 
• So (इसलिए): Used to indicate a result or consequence, not appropriate for simultaneous actions.
 
• Thus (इस प्रकार): Used to summarize or conclude, not appropriate for ongoing simultaneous actions.
